title: Wickapogue (Meacox Bay)
summary: Wickapogue is a farming district at the western end of Meacox Bay in Southampton. The name is interpreted as at the end of the pond or water-place.
history_content: The name appears in Southampton land-division records and remained attached to the Meacox Bay landscape. Dated records appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Weequapaug, Weekapaug, Wecapoug, Wickapogue, and Wickapog. The name is interpreted as at the end of the pond or water-place.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names contain knowledge of the landscape and encode unique perceptions of landscapes with which Indigenous Peoples have interacted for hundreds, often thousands, of years.”

— Rebekah R. Ingram and Kahente Horn-Miller, Mapping for Reconnection: Place Name Documentation and the Atlas of Kanyen'kehá:ka Space (2024), Abstract, first sentence
preservation_content: Wickapogue preserves a Meacox Bay placename that marks the end or limit of a water-place within Southampton land history.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker at the western Meacox Bay / Wickapogue district. This is not an exact 1668 allotment coordinate.
